Philip Bart was a longtime Communist Party member and official. He served as the Party's Organizational Secretary (ca. 1963), and as the head of the History Commission (ca. 1979). The majority of this collection consists of clippings from the Communist Party Press, namely the Daily Worker, the Worker, and the Daily World, along with clippings from other periodicals. There is also a small amount of printed ephemera. Materials in this subseries focus on the growth of anti-communism after World War II, the political and legal attacks on the Communist Party and its members, the role of the House Un-American Activities Committee and the Subversive Activities Control Board, and the U.S. government's loyalty oath program.
